documentation.overview: JSON Web Token (JWT) is an open, industry-standard RFC 7519 method for securely representing claims between two parties. Compact, URL-safe, and cryptographically signed using either a secret (HMAC) or a public/private key pair (RSA or ECDSA).
documentation.purpose: Stateless authentication, authorization claim passing, single sign-on (SSO), and secure data exchange in modern microservices.
documentation.configuration: Configure signing algorithms (RS256, EdDSA, HS256), token expiration (expiresIn), issuer (iss), and audience (aud).
documentation.security_considerations: Never store sensitive data (passwords, credit cards) in JWT payloads because payloads are only base64url-encoded and can be read by anyone. Always sign with asymmetric algorithms (RS256 or Ed25519) in distributed systems and keep expiration lifetimes short.
documentation.error_handling: Handle `TokenExpiredError` to prompt client token refresh and `JsonWebTokenError` for signature forgery detection.

symbols.name: jwt.sign
symbols.syntax: jwt.sign(payload: string | Buffer | object, secretOrPrivateKey: Secret, options?: SignOptions): string
symbols.description: Signs a payload and returns the compact encoded JWT string with header, payload, and signature components separated by dots.

parameters.name: payload
parameters.description: User claims or session metadata to serialize into the token body.

parameters.name: secretOrPrivateKey
parameters.description: Cryptographic key used to compute the digital signature.

symbols.name: jwt.verify
symbols.syntax: jwt.verify(token: string, secretOrPublicKey: Secret, options?: VerifyOptions): JwtPayload | string
symbols.description: Verifies the cryptographic signature of the token and decodes the payload, rejecting expired or tampered tokens.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The raw incoming Bearer token string.
